summary:
# NOTES: THE GREAT WHITE ARMY (Max Pemberton, Cassell 1916; single book, 10 chapters)

## Frame
- Author's note: Napoleon's Grand Army invaded Russia June 1812; 600,000 crossed the Niemen; ~20,000 "famished, frost-bitten spectres" crossed the Bridge of Kovno in December.
- Narrator: Janil de Constant, Surgeon-Major of the Guard (Vélites), veteran, ex-professor at Univ. of Paris. Fled Paris 1792, lived Leipsic, taught French, studied medicine. Narrates as an old man in Paris.
- Nephew: Captain Léon de Courcelles, Vélites, handsome, womanizer, impetuous. Servant: Gascogne.
- Recurring: Emperor pinches Constant's ear when pleased. "Little Corporal." Constant calls the army "we"; ends many chapters with Paris/Léon jokes.

## Principal characters
- **Valerie St. Antoine**: beautiful, French-born, raised Russian. Brother René (sent to St. Petersburg). Ward of Prince Nicholas. Father Colonel St. Antoine (Chasseurs of the Line, Second Battalion), Nice-born, left in Terror. Mother d. Poland 5 yrs earlier. Speaks Russian. Repeatedly rescues the French; later rides as hussar.
- **Prince Nicholas**: son of Prince Boris; Russian officer (white uniform, black cuirass); sworn vendetta on French; Guillotine sadist. Loses arm at elbow to his own guillotine (ch II). Carried off Valerie in ch I.
- **Prince Boris**: owner of Moscow house; Orthodox, permitted Catholic secret chapel; left Moscow for Nishni.
- **François**: steward/lackey, killed Valerie's brother (ch I).
- **Heriot**: dandy at Moscow house, snuffbox edged in diamonds; claims left Paris with Count of Provence 1790.
- **Sergeant Bourgogne**: Vélites, Moscow & Slawkowo.
- **Sergeant Bardot** (Gustav): Fusiliers, nicknamed "the antelope"; climbs rope in ch II; plunders brandy/flour; killed in ch X.
- **Gascogne**: Léon's servant.
- **Zayde** (or Zoida): golden-haired girl, 17, Eastern/mixed, in wood with treasure; no French. Léon's love; later hidden.
- **Prince Karasin**: Tartar, murdered; owner of treasure.
- **Captain Payard**: dragoons, fat, curly-haired, blue eyes; secretly eats from Russian camp; killed by Tcharnhoff.
- **Madame Pauline**: Frenchwoman, Russian officer's wife, red hair, Cossack green uniform; lover Colonel Ferdinand Tcharnhoff (dragoons, 35, Tartar-faced); Pauline kills him.
- **Madame Zchekofsky**: old hawk, ermine, diamonds, Liadoui; daughter **Kyra**, prophetess, who foretold Moscow burning.
- **Petrovka**: girl guide, boyish, from Druobona, feigns no French; farmer **Serges** (moujik); daughter **Anna** actually fired barn; Petrovka shields her.
- **Major Duhesne** (chasseurs à cheval), **Captains Legard and Fournier** (fusiliers): judges in Petrovka trial.
- **Isidore**: young Jew guide at Bobr; wife (unnamed) helpful, haggling; robber **Orlof**.
- **Joan d'Izambert**: 14, silver-fox furs, nobly born; brother **Gabriel d'Izambert** (pontonnier, delirious, finds ford, dies in river); father **General d'Izambert** (engineers, old, widower).
- **Gros-Jean**: Vélites, dies at Bérézina.
- **Merry old gentleman**: Polish-looking, four-horse sleigh, takes Valerie & Joan; Elbing prefect **Herrn Immo von Gustorf**.
- **Colonel Bourgoriau**: fusiliers at Bérézina.
- Historical: Ney, Murat, Eugène, Davoust, Dumesnil, Roguet, Kutusoff, General Volska, Marshal Berthier/Mortier/Lefebvre.

## CH I: THE WOMAN ON THE STAIRS
- 14 Sept: enter Moscow; Mont du Salut 3:30pm. Léon rode with Major Pavart (chasseurs). Constant with Bourgogne.
- Governor released convicts, who hold palace.
- Heriot grabs Constant's bridle: "be good enough to come into yonder house." Gate barred with iron bars.
- Young artist from Fréjus (dead, shot in back, pistol at side) in "service of my lord, the prince." Heriot: "shot himself." Constant: "Men do not shoot themselves in the middle of the back!"
- Voices. Constant pushes Heriot ahead; lackey throat slit. Three convicts in sheepskins, torches. Constant pistol-butts first; they flee.
- Constant alone; shutters; Italian garden; balcony; bells of Moscow; night.
- Assassins return ~10pm. Valerie (white and silver robe) appears on staircase with candle. "I am Valerie… François the steward killed him."
- Hidden oratory with golden lamp, eastern turret; axes at door.
- Escape up cupola gallery, 80 ft; Léon on white horse below; Constant shouts unheard.
- Constant shoots shaggy head; street soldiers fire on tower. Second face pistol-butted.
- Chapel burned; Constant kills torch man, other falls down stairs.
- Mob looting, "Fire!" Library; locked antechamber; Nicholas opens; Valerie kisses him.
- Officers: "A spy!" Blindfolded; mock volley; Constant faints; woman's laughter. Nicholas carries Valerie off.
- Léon finds Constant at wall. "A welcome to Moscow!"

## CH II: THE GUILLOTINE
- Moscow deserted; looting; fires daily; convicts blamed.
- Valerie writes Léon invitation to dinner beyond suburbs. Léon initially refuses, then goes (28 Sept). Five officers lost that week.
- Constant hires droshky under threat ("hanged at the gate of the Kremlin"). Bardot accompanies.
- Route: north road to Petersburg; Ivan's Tower on island in pool; drawbridge; sentry drunk; Bardot crawls; neither can swim.
- Valerie crosses in crazy boat; disappears. Constant & Bardot take boat.
- Léon's account: dinner in round tower, black velvet walls, scaffold with rushes, headless trunk. Russian Guard officers (Count Rafalovitch). Gold dishes. Valerie's face behind curtain.
- Nicholas: father in Paris 1794; friend Chevalier Constantini executed Place de la Grève; guillotine model by Dr. Guillotin.
- Constant & Bardot kill sentry (into moat). Bardot climbs rope, fires, strikes great bell; lowers bridge.
- Cossacks thunder; Bardot's shot distracts; mock Revolution-theatre scaffold, Tartar executioner. Léon: "I congratulate the Prince of the Assassins." Nicholas: "You murdered twenty thousand honest people." Blade cuts Nicholas's arm at elbow.
- Valerie summons Léon's Red Hussar troop by droshky. Léon wakes: "Where is Valerie St. Antoine?"

## CH III: THE TREASURE IN THE WOODS
- 18 Oct: news of leaving Moscow; left 19 Oct. Constant's gold plate from Ivan's Cross.
- Mile from Smolensk road; Léon & Constant meet Zayde in pit with Cossack (misfire, Cossack flees).
- Treasure ~half million francs: pearls, emeralds, gold Indian images, ermine, sable, Damascus scabbards.
- Zayde: 17, golden hair, blue silk breeches, white-and-gold coat, Austrian hussar kepi, ermine cloak. Léon kisses her within 20 min.
- Wrecked coach: old man shot, coachman stabbed. Treasure = Prince Karasin's (Tartar, murdered by servants).
- Monastery: gilt dome, brown-habited monks, prior with gold cross, sour refectory keeper, fiery spirit drugs Constant & Léon.
- Léon proposes marriage to Zayde ("What is marriage, my uncle?").
- Constant wakes near midnight in glade. Léon with Red Hussars.
- Monastery barred; sends 6 hussars for field piece (half battery from Ney's rearguard); gun brings down door.
- Monastery empty; secret passage hunt fails.
- Cossacks (3,000) chase; "En avant!"; Cossack sabred by Constant.
- Bivouac fires = monks' fires; Zayde & shorn "monk" (Cossack) by fire flee.
- Constant told story in Paris 1813; newspapers: "A squadron of hussars saved by a flight of monks!"

## CH IV: PHANTOM MUSIC
- Snow began 29 Oct. Cold beyond imagining. Dead along road.
- Wrecked yellow berline; coachman frozen. Baroness de Nivois & granddaughter (15) dead; Valerie alive.
- Valerie: father alive, serves Emperor. Constant recalls "Colonel St. Antoine, Second Battalion Chasseurs of the Line."
- Léon gives cloak to Valerie; Constant buries women with sappers.
- Slawkowo: town full of troops; church; organ plays "On va leur percer les flancs." Léon: "your ears playing tricks."
- Sergeant Bourgogne: "Let the Guard go elsewhere… we reported you for dead."
- Church: ~500 men; horse meat; fires in chancel (screen panels burned) and nave.
- Valerie's history told. Wants to see Emperor; plans of General Kutusoff.
- Cossack alarm; friendly fire: chasseurs of the line, 40 dead.
- Colonel St. Antoine dies at dawn. Valerie burns papers: "Your army shall perish!"
- Constant & Léon to Emperor (Murat, Dumesnil present). Emperor: "If you do not find her I will have you shot."
- Church empty; search; Valerie gone. Constant returns; "His Majesty left at one o'clock… there was a woman with him."

## CH V: THE CAMP BY THE RIVER
- Captain Payard (dragoons) secretly eats Russian food; "bon camarade, I steal from the Russians." Invites Constant & Léon.
- Frozen valley; Cossack patrol; Vitzala village (General Volska's camp). Pauline's hut.
- Pauline: tall, red hair, Cossack green uniform. Toast "France… our safe return!"
- Servant: "Colonel Tcharnhoff returned!" Tcharnhoff: Tartar face, pig eyes, white dragoon uniform.
- Tcharnhoff: Major Royate tied to tree; Lt. de Duras burned at Letizka. "Two of you shall go… five minutes by the clock."
- Payard lunges; Tcharnhoff shoots Payard dead across table; Pauline stabs Tcharnhoff. "I will say that you killed him. Go!"
- Run through snow; wolves kill Léon's horse & Constant's; woodlander's hut; Red Hussars rescue. Constant met Pauline June 1813, Rue de Rivoli.

## CH VI: THE WITCH IN ERMINE
- Emperor walks with grenadiers; cantinière's baby dies.
- Liadoui post-house; Emperor sends Constant to dinner at Madame Zchekofsky's (wood house, Sèvres, tapestries). Sturgeon, caviar, Burgundy.
- Emperor asks for Kyra. Constant skeptical. Emperor goes into Kyra's chapel (Madonna, lamp).
- Sentinel murdered; Cossacks come. Constant on bed, feigned hysterical laughter; sings "Ram, ram, ram…"
- Drink; Cossacks drunk. Constant wears Emperor's cloak and cocked hat; captured by Cossacks.
- Constant wakes among Red Hussars: "You got very drunk." Emperor "six leagues on the road to Wilna."
- Madame & Kyra seen Paris 1815.

## CH VII: LITTLE PETROVKA
- 25 Nov, morning; Emperor on foot with baton, red velvet cap black fox trim; Murat & Eugène either side; Berthier, Ney, Mortier, Lefebvre behind.
- Russian battery; Ney charges Cossacks; Kutusoff withdraws, failing to strike.
- Léon's captive: Petrovka, 17-ish boy-garb, from Druobona. Léon plans to take her to her father's house; 150 men follow.
- Dark ravine; farmhouse of moujik Serges. Petrovka: "This is the house of… Serges."
- Barn with 150 men; fire; locked bars; 30 men dragged out burned.
- Chasseur accuses Petrovka; trial by Constant, Léon, Legard, Fournier, Duhesne. Vote: death.
- Léon draws sword; twenty men seize Petrovka; she is dragged to beech tree.
- Cossacks charge; Petrovka's friends. "I never believed that they would kill me."
- Petrovka: "I give you your lives… do not forget little Petrovka." Anna (farmer's daughter) fired the barn; Petrovka knew all along.

## CH VIII: THE AFFAIR AT THE POST-HOUSE
- Constant & Léon lost on road to Bérézina; Bardot not present. Constant's arm pierced by lance.
- Léon shoots Cossack leader in face; chasseur à pied (Châlons, wife & children) kills Cossack, dies.
- Cossack capes & busbies disguise.
- Post-house: French flee; Valerie there: "The Emperor is at Bobr. He is a little tired of me, mon ami."
- Russian cavalry officers arrive; Valerie fools them; Léon nearly roasted on stove; 500 Russians enter village, ~250 dead, ~250 captured.
- Kutusoff's aide-de-camp dead: papers say Bérézina bridge held by Russians. Valerie reads.
- Ney: dispatch to Emperor; squadron escort dismissed.
- Lost in defile; cottage of Isidore & wife (Jewish); "Your husband has been out to rob the soldiers"; 100 francs promised.
- Robbers at cave: fusilier officer beheaded; Isidore shoots third; takes gold.
- Lost in ravine; shrine; Bobr. Valerie seen riding a hussar's horse in Bobr street.

## CH IX: WE CROSS THE BÉRÉZINA
- Bridge news; Borisoff; night of Nov 20 at priest's house.
- Joan d'Izambert: "Sergeant Picard sent me to you." Garden arbour; General d'Izambert; Gabriel delirious: "The bridge!"
- Gabriel found ford below Studianka, four miles above old bridge. Father: "Save my son, major, and you may yet save France."
- Valerie: "Go… let the Emperor know. I will stay with these people."
- Emperor arrives; Gabriel in baggage wagon; ford assumed.
- Pontoniers work in river, Emperor serves wine.
- Morning: Russians bombard; crowds of camp followers; bridges jammed.
- Gros-Jean dies (Cuirassier thrusts him down).
- 5pm: Gabriel: "I am to blow up the bridge… the others must perish."
- Constant decides to swim: horse with Joan on saddle-bow; Valerie on black charger; father stays with Gabriel.
- Swim; ice; corpses; reach shore. Bridge blown. Constant "sees" Gabriel and father in river (fancy).
- Bivouac of Colonel Bourgoriau's fusiliers; Emperor at farmhouse nearby.

## CH X: THE LAST REVIEW
- 12,000 corpses recovered in spring; ~30,000 left to Kovno.
- Emperor left Smorgoni 5 Dec; Murat in command. Vilna plundered.
- Party: Constant, Valerie, Léon, Joan, Sergeant Bardot (Vilna brandy & flour).
- Lost near Niemen; Polish farm (widow, two sons); night attack; Bardot shot/cut, dies.
- Old merry gentleman with sleigh & 80 lancers (Lithuanian) takes Valerie & Joan; Constant & Léon bound.
- Cellar at village; German-speaking sergeant offers parole; Elbing.
- Elbing ~10pm; prison; young Captain; charge: "rendering help to the Emperor's enemies and robbing French soldiers," laid by prefect Herrn Immo von Gustorf.
- Night in tower cell; drums and cheers at dawn: French enter Elbing.
- Young captain takes them to prefect's house; Valerie is mistress (prefect fled).
- Survivors: 22,000 of 600,000. Last review: Marshal Ney says troubles over; sledges to French frontier.
- Last line: "The day of battle was over; the night of our sorry victory had been won."
